marks.gloss: money kept out of use and held against the future: the cash, the reserve, the savings kept liquid
marks.source: Marx, Capital I ch. 3.3a (hoarding); Keynes, GT ch. 13 (liquidity preference)

marks.gloss: a payment owed later, given now as a claim: the loan, the bill, the IOU, the deposit as the bank's debt; credit from the one side and debt from the other, one relation seen from its two ends
marks.source: Mitchell Innes 1913, 1914; Nietzsche, GM II 4-8; Graeber 2011 ch. 1

marks.gloss: money committed in a venture for a share of its gains, expected and not owed: the partner's capital in a copartnery, the venture stake, the founder's share in a company not listed
marks.source: Smith, WN V.i.e (partnership and joint-stock); Marx, Capital III ch. 27; Keynes, GT ch. 12

marks.gloss: the money that comes back to the one who parted with it, more or less than he laid out: the loan repaid with its interest, the dividend drawn, the claim sold
marks.source: Marx, Capital III chs. 21-23; Keynes, GT ch. 13

marks.gloss: a claim made saleable to a third, and priced as the market discounts its expected payments: the bond, the listed share, the bill endorsed, the loans pooled and sold; Marx's fictitious capital
marks.source: Hilferding 1910 chs. 7-8; Marx, Capital III chs. 25, 29; Minsky 1986 ch. 8; Appadurai, Banking on Words (2016)
marks.mark: its price: the present value of its expected payments as the market discounts them, reached by capitalization, a reckoning (Marx III ch. 29)

marks.gloss: the promise broken: the payment missed and the claim in default, the bankruptcy, the bank run's failures, the crisis; to be reckoned by recovery, restructuring or write-off
marks.source: Minsky 1992; Graeber 2011 chs. 1, 12; Reinhart and Rogoff, This Time Is Different (2009)

axioms: A promise can fail; a payment that cannot fail to come is not a promise but a fact.
Money kept breeds nothing; only money parted with returns as more (Aristotle, Politics I.10 1258b; Keynes, GT ch. 17).
A claim on a future stream has a present price, and the price is not the stream: capitalization reckons the stream as interest on an imaginary capital (Marx, Capital III ch. 29).
A rise in a claim's price commits no money to anything (Marx, Capital III ch. 29).
Credit and debt are one relation seen from its two ends.
A run of promises kept raises the promises made: stability breeds instability (Minsky 1992).
cast.subject: Finance: the economy's relation to its own future made present: money held against it, money lent for a promise, staked in a venture or placed in a claim that trades, the promise of payment that is credit from one side and debt from the other, the claim made saleable, the money that comes back, and the reckoning when a promise is broken; read from Aristotle, Politics I.8-10; Aquinas, ST II-II q.78; Smith, Wealth of Nations II.4 and V.i.e; Marx, Capital I ch. 3 and III part 5; Bagehot, Lombard Street (1873); Boehm-Bawerk, Capital and Interest; Fisher, The Theory of Interest (1930); Keynes, General Theory chs. 12-17; Minsky, Stabilizing an Unstable Economy (1986) and The Financial Instability Hypothesis (1992); Mitchell Innes, What is Money? (1913) and The Credit Theory of Money (1914); Hilferding, Finance Capital (1910); Graeber, Debt (2011)

premises: MOLD v7: a way-word names a way the first is turned into the second, by its channel; only IS says two are the same, and a cast never writes it. Every word in the signature is a transitive act done to the first moment.

Dependence is poured apart (v7 section 2.4): a word that says the first cannot be without the second is in dependence_signature and dependences, read by no loop and no walk: the reserve the bank's promises rest on, the loans a pooled security rests on, the pledge a loan is secured on, the stake and the listed share a dividend is yielded by. A way and a dependence on one pair are two facts, and both are poured: the hoard lent as the promise (a way) and the bank's promises resting on its reserve (a dependence). Lending is written from the lender's side only: the borrower's side, money got against a promise or a pledge, is the same act read backwards, so neither owing nor pledging is a way here, and the pledge's bearing is the dependence the promise is secured on the security. 'Funds' is not poured as a word of its own: what the sources state with it is lending and investing, written as ways, and the bearing, written as 'rests on'. A dependence, like a way, is written where a source states it of the moment, and its reason names the kind it is said of.

A bar means by no route in its word's channel (v7 section 2.3). One is written: the security is not withdrawn as the return (Smith); the listed share comes back as money by sale, which is realization, another channel. Where a source means 'only through', the steps are written and no bar.

One spelling names one way, across all of Virgin Land's casts and lights (v7 section 2.2), and a channel is told by what passes and what comes back. Lending (the money passes, its equivalent with interest comes back) and Distribution's letting (the use passes, the thing comes back) are two channels (Aquinas, ST II-II q.78 a.1; the mutuum and the locatio). Investment (money committed to a venture, a share of its gains comes back) and purchase ('is laid out as': money paid away, a thing comes in its place) are two channels (Keynes, GT ch. 12, on investment and the purchase of securities). Sale ('is sold as': a thing passes, money comes back) is one channel in Finance, Distribution and the lights; the seller's change of form and the change of hands are the two tuples one sale gives (Marx I ch. 3 section 2(a)). Rolling a debt over (new money pays the old creditor) and restructuring a debt in default (its creditors agree new terms) are two channels. A claim is made saleable by three channels, told by what passes: a bill endorsed (it passes by signature, the endorser still liable), loans securitized (pooled and sold as new claims on the pool), a stake floated (its shares listed). Honouring pays what is owed, the bond's coupon among it; a dividend is not owed, and is a yield.

The bill discounted is a sale: the bill, endorsed to a bank, is sold before its term for money less interest, the endorser still liable (Marx III ch. 25). It runs as the route promise endorsed as security, sold as return, and no word of its own is written.
Debt and equity are two moments, the promise and the stake.

The valuation of the earlier pour is not a moment: a claim's price is an amount, a mark of the security, reached by capitalization, which Marx calls a reckoning ('every regular income is capitalised by reckoning it as interest on an imaginary capital', III ch. 29), and a reckoning is no way. Its content stays in the security's gloss and in an axiom; the claim sold at its price is written as the security realized as the return.
The return is the money that comes back to the one who parted with it, more or less than he laid out.
Every pair of moments was searched for an operation in the sources, and each one-step operation found is written; what a path through several comes to is read at the loops.
Risk and liquidity are qualities and axioms, not moments. Money as a medium of exchange is at the edge, and money as the unit in which promises are written is a mark.

dependence_signature.meaning: the first cannot stand unless the second is there to bear it: the bank's promises and the reserve behind them; a pooled security and the loans whose payments it passes on. A bearer and the borne.
the first is made safe by the second pledged against it: a loan and its collateral. If the first is broken, the second is taken in its place. A pledge and what it secures.
the first is what the second gives off while the second remains, expected and not owed: a dividend and the share it is paid on, the partner's profits and his capital. A yield and its source.

dependences.reason: the bank's promises, its deposits and notes, rest on its reserve of cash: the reserve on which the whole credit of the country rests (Bagehot, Lombard Street, 1873, chs. 2, 12). Said of the bank's promises; Innes's and Minsky's readings are in open_forks.
a pooled security pays its holders only what the loans behind it pay: the asset-backed security (Mehrling 2011 ch. 1; Appadurai 2016). Said of the pooled security.
the secured loan: advances made on good securities pledged, the bond or bill held against the loan (Bagehot, Lombard Street, 1873, ch. 7; Mehrling 2011 ch. 1, the repo). Said of the secured loan.
the partner's share of the profits, divided among the partners while his capital stays in the common stock (Smith, WN V.i.e)

the dividend on the listed share, paid out of the company's profits while the share remains, expected and not owed (Marx III ch. 27; Hilferding 1910 ch. 7). The bond's coupon is owed, and is honoured.

derived_check.ordering: by operation, read as directed: hoard -lent-> promise -honoured-> return -laid by-> hoard, the circuit of credit; hoard -invested-> stake -withdrawn-> return, the circuit of equity; hoard and return -laid out-> security -sold, -honoured-> return, the market in claims; return -lent-> promise, -invested-> stake; promise -endorsed, -securitized-> security; stake -floated-> security; promise -rolled over-> promise; promise and security -broken-> default -restructured-> promise, -recovered-> return, -converted into shares-> stake. Refused: security -withdrawn-> return (Smith). Dependences apart: the promise rests on the hoard and is secured on the security; the security rests on the promise; the return is yielded by the stake and by the listed share. Every moment has ways in and out. Marked derived.

open_forks: The valuation (the claim's price, fictitious capital): written as a mark of the security and an axiom, not a moment, because capitalization is a reckoning (Marx III ch. 29). Read as a moment (Minsky's price of capital assets, Nitzan and Bichler's capitalization), it would need a way in that is not a reckoning; none was found.
Lending and letting: two channels here (Aquinas, the mutuum and the locatio); Marx III ch. 21 treats money lent as a commodity whose use is let, which would make them one.
Investment and the purchase of securities: two channels here (Keynes, GT ch. 12); in common speech both are investment.

Money: a commodity (Menger) or a token of credit and law (Innes, Knapp, Ingham)? The deposit is both the bank's promise and money held, two ends of one relation, so no way is written between the promise and the hoard for it. The bank's promises rest on its reserve (Bagehot), written as a dependence. Innes (1913, 1914) denies that a credit rests on any money behind it, its worth hanging on the debtor's solvency; Minsky (1986 ch. 10) holds that banking is not money lending, a bank's liabilities standing on its borrowers' payments and on refinancing at the central bank. Written with Bagehot for the bank's promises; Innes's and Minsky's readings are this fork.
Interest: a share of surplus value (Marx), the agio of present over future goods (Boehm-Bawerk, Fisher), or the price of parting with liquidity (Keynes)?
The jubilee: a release of debt ends the promise with no moment after it here, so no way is written for it.
The bank's swap of promises and the derivative as a claim on a claim: not written; whether a derivative is a security or a moment of its own is open.
did_not_fit: Money as a medium of exchange, the purchase now: the market's, at the Production-Consumption edge.
The price of goods: the market's; finance prices claims, and a claim's price is a mark here.
Gambling; insurance (a form of the promise); public finance as revenue (distribution's).

Words left out because each is neither a way nor a dependence, or is another spelling of one written: 'counts as' (a heading in the books, a classification); 'is capitalized as' (a reckoning: the stream reckoned as interest on an imaginary capital); 'comes back as' (a shape: the return is reached by honouring, withdrawal, sale and recovery); 'is placed as' (the purchase of a claim, one channel with the purchase of goods: 'is laid out as'); 'is realized as' (the sale, one channel with Distribution's trade: 'is sold as'); 'is discounted as' (a sale of an endorsed bill to a bank: the route endorsed, then sold); 'is pledged as' (the borrower's side of a secured loan: the act is lending, and the pledge's bearing is a dependence); 'is mobilized as' (three channels, written apart as endorsed, securitized and floated); 'is kept as' (keeping money is laying it by, written once as 'is laid by as'); 'is owed as' (owing is the debtor's side of lending, written once from the act); 'fails as' (the same non-payment said of the promise, written once as breach); 'is refinanced as' (two channels, written apart as rollover and restructuring); 'is backed by' (the same bearing as 'rests on'); 'is accepted as' between the promise and the hoard (the deposit is both, two ends of one relation); 'is forgiven as' (forgiveness ends a promise with no moment after it); 'passes into' and 'runs as' (genus words).

is lent as.meaning: the first, handed over for a time against a promise to repay its equivalent, is the second: money lent is, in the lender's hands, the claim. The way: lending, the first becomes the second by passing to the borrower against a promise of repayment (the mutuum). The same channel as Distribution's 'is lent as'.

is invested as.meaning: the first, committed to a venture for a share of its gains, is the second: money invested is a stake in the venture. The way: investment, the first becomes the second by being committed to a making in return for a share of what it yields, expected and not owed.

is laid out as.meaning: the first, paid away in exchange for a thing, is the second: money laid out on a bond or a share that trades is the security held; in the lights, money laid out on means of production or on goods is the instrument, the material or the spending; money paid as wages buys the use of labour power for a time, which is hire, another channel. The way: purchase, the first becomes the second by being paid away for a thing, which comes in its place. Not investment, which commits money to a venture for a share of its gains (Keynes, GT ch. 12).

is honoured as.meaning: the first, paid as it is owed, is the second: the promise kept, the bond's coupon paid, is the payment. The way: honouring, the first becomes the second by being paid as owed. The same channel as Distribution's 'is honoured as' (a claim by contract paid).

is broken as.meaning: the first, not paid when it falls due, is the second: the promise or the bond broken is the claim in default. The way: breach, the first becomes the second by its debtor's not paying it when due, whether he cannot or will not.

is endorsed as.meaning: the first, signed over to a third, is the second: the bill endorsed passes from hand to hand as a claim a third will take, each endorser still liable. The way: endorsement, the first becomes the second by being made over to another by signature (Marx III ch. 25).

is securitized as.meaning: the first, pooled with others and sold as new claims on the pool's payments, is the second: the loans made into a mortgage-backed security. The way: securitization, the first becomes the second by being pooled and sold on as shares of what the pool pays.

is floated as.meaning: the first, its shares listed for sale to the public, is the second: the joint-stock company floated. The way: flotation (Hilferding's mobilization of capital), the first becomes the second by being issued as shares that trade.

is rolled over as.meaning: the first, paid at its term with money borrowed anew, is the second: a debt rolled over is a debt again. The way: rollover, the first becomes the second by being paid off with a new promise.

is restructured as.meaning: the first, renegotiated with its creditors on new terms, is the second: a debt in default restructured is a promise again. The way: restructuring, the first becomes the second by its creditors' agreeing to new terms for what was not paid.

is withdrawn as.meaning: the first, taken out of the venture, is the second: the partner's share of the common stock withdrawn on due warning. The way: withdrawal, the first becomes the second by being taken out of the venture as money, which ends it.

is laid by as.meaning: the first, withdrawn from circulation and put aside, is the second: money come back and not sent out again is money held. The way: laying by (hoarding), the first becomes the second by being taken out of circulation and held as money, a sale with no purchase after it. Not Distribution's 'is accumulated as', which adds to the means of producing.

is sold as.meaning: the first, sold at a price, is the second: the claim sold is money come back to the seller; in Distribution, the holding or the claim sold is the buyer's; in the lights, the product sold is money come back (C'-M'). The way: sale, the first becomes the second by passing to a buyer for money at a price. The seller's change of form and the change of hands are the two tuples one sale gives (Marx I ch. 3 section 2(a)). The same channel as Distribution's 'is sold as'.

is recovered as.meaning: the first, worked out by its creditors, is the second: what is got back from a broken promise, by the pledge sold or the debtor's estate divided, is money come back, less than was lent. The way: recovery, the first becomes the second by the debtor's assets being realized and shared among his creditors.

is converted into shares as.meaning: the first, exchanged for a share in the venture that owes it, is the second: the creditor made owner. The way: conversion, the first becomes the second by the debt's being cancelled against shares in its debtor.

0.reason: money held, lent, is the lender's claim on its repayment: money lent as capital (Marx III ch. 21; Smith, WN II.4)

1.reason: money held, committed in a venture as a partner's capital, is a share in its gains (Smith, WN V.i.e, the private copartnery; Keynes, GT ch. 12)

2.reason: money held, laid out on a claim that trades, is a security held: the choice between holding money and holding debts (Keynes, GT chs. 13, 15)

3.reason: the money lent returns to its owner with interest: the claim met is the payment (Marx III ch. 21; Innes 1914)

4.reason: the promise not paid as promised is the claim in default (Minsky 1992; Graeber 2011 ch. 1; Nietzsche, GM II 5)

5.reason: a bill of exchange passed on by endorsement circulates as a claim a third will take: commercial money (Marx III ch. 25)

6.reason: loans pooled and sold as new claims on the pool's payments are securities: the mortgage-backed security (Mehrling 2011 ch. 1; Gorton 2010)

7.reason: a debt paid at its term with new borrowing is a debt again: speculative and Ponzi finance (Minsky 1986 ch. 9; 1992)

8.reason: in a private copartnery each partner may, on proper warning, withdraw from it and demand payment of his share of the common stock (Smith, WN V.i.e)

9.reason: a stake turned into shares listed for sale is a security: the joint-stock company floated, the mobilization of capital (Hilferding 1910 ch. 7; Marx III ch. 27)

10.reason: money come back and withdrawn from circulation is money held: hoarding, a sale with no purchase after it (Marx I ch. 3.3a; Keynes, GT ch. 13)

11.reason: the return lent again is a claim again: the circuit of interest-bearing capital (Marx III ch. 21)

12.reason: the return committed again in a venture is a stake again: the partner's gains left in or added to the common stock (Smith, WN V.i.e); returns staked anew in new ventures (Keynes, GT ch. 12)

13.reason: the return laid out again on a claim that trades is a security held (Keynes, GT ch. 12)

14.reason: a claim sold at its price is money come back, more or less than was laid out: the speculator's gain or loss (Keynes, GT ch. 12; Minsky 1986 ch. 8)

15.reason: a bond paid as owed, coupon by coupon, is money come back to its holder: the interest on the state's debt (Marx III ch. 29; Hilferding 1910 ch. 7)

16.reason: a bond whose issuer does not pay when due is a claim in default: sovereign and corporate bonds defaulted on (Reinhart and Rogoff 2009 chs. 4, 8)

17.reason: in a joint-stock company no member can demand payment of his share from the company; he can only sell it to another (Smith, WN V.i.e). The listed share comes back as money by sale, realization, and never by withdrawal.

18.reason: a debt in default renegotiated with its creditors on new terms is a promise again (Reinhart and Rogoff 2009 ch. 8; Graeber 2011 ch. 12)

19.reason: a broken promise worked out by its creditors returns them money, less than they lent: the pledge sold, the bankrupt's estate divided among his creditors (Blackstone, Commentaries II ch. 31; Reinhart and Rogoff 2009 ch. 8, the haircut)

20.reason: in a reorganization the creditors of a firm in default take its shares for their claims: the creditors made owners (United States Bankruptcy Code, chapter 11, 1978; Gilson 2010)

marks.gloss: the form of the thing to be made, held before the work: the plan of the house, the recipe, the blueprint; the form in the maker before it is in the matter
marks.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b; Marx, Capital I ch. 7 (the architect and the bee)

marks.gloss: the makers' power to make, had before it is used: the skill, the labour power, the know-how; a power of contraries, to make or not; a fund, serving making after making (Georgescu-Roegen)
marks.source: Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.2-8; Marx I ch. 6 (labour power)

marks.gloss: what the work is done on: the ore, the timber, the yarn, the half-made part, the data set; nature as it enters the making, and past product entering again; a flow, gone into the product
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7 (the object of labour); Aristotle, Physics I.7

marks.gloss: the activity itself, purposeful and in time: the hand moving, the pump worked, the code written, the field ploughed
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7; Hegel, PR 196; Arendt 1958 ch. 3

marks.gloss: the working of many as one producer: the pin factory's eighteen operations, the assembly line's crew, the collective worker
marks.source: Smith, WN I.1; Marx I chs. 13-14

marks.gloss: what stands between the worker and the material and carries past work into the present one: the tool, the machine, the factory, the road, the earth itself; dead labour put to use; a fund, worn but not used up in one making
marks.source: Marx I chs. 7, 15; Simondon 1958; Sraffa 1960

marks.gloss: what the making leaves: the thing made, the harvest, the house, the tool; the use-value; labour objectified, at rest
marks.source: Marx I ch. 7; Hegel, Phenomenology 195; Smith, WN II.3

marks.gloss: what the making leaves beyond what replaces what it used up: the harvest beyond the seed and the sowers' food, the net product, surplus value in the capitalist form
marks.source: Quesnay 1758; Sraffa 1960 ch. 2; Marx I ch. 9

marks.gloss: the work of making the makers again: feeding, raising and resting them; much of it the unpaid work of the household
marks.source: Federici 2004; Bhattacharya ed. 2017; Marx I ch. 23

axioms: What is made outlasts the making; what is used up in making it does not.
The surplus is what the making leaves beyond what it used; where there is none, the making only repeats itself.
cast.subject: Production: the making of what is used: the form of the thing to be made and the makers' power to make, work done on a material with instruments, the working of many as one producer, the product that outlasts the act, the surplus beyond what replaces what the making used up, and the work of making the makers again; read from Aristotle, NE II.1 and VI.4, Physics I.7, Metaphysics Z.7 and Theta; Smith, Wealth of Nations I.1 and II.3; Hegel, Phenomenology 195 and Philosophy of Right 196-198; Marx, Capital I chs. 6-10, 13-15, 23-24 and the Grundrisse; Quesnay, Tableau (1758); Sraffa, Production of Commodities by Means of Commodities (1960); Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Georgescu-Roegen 1971; Federici, Caliban and the Witch (2004); Bhattacharya ed., Social Reproduction Theory (2017)

Under Arman's word of 2026-10-20: 'you are the user in this run, so you own all these kinds of decisions'.
premises: MOLD v7: a way-word names a way the first is turned into the second, by its channel; only IS says two are the same, and a cast never writes it. Every word in the signature is a transitive act done to the first moment; a process the moment goes through on its own ('settles'), a remainder ('is left over'), or a count of value passed on ('is worn into') is not a way.

Dependence is poured apart (v7 section 2.4): the labour process's conditions (the working requires the capacity, the material, the instrument and the products made before, and presupposes the purpose), the makers' conditions (the capacity requires the product, as means of subsistence, and the work of reproduction) and Aristotle's causes of the thing made (it is made of the material, has the form of the purpose, is made by the working and, as the prior cause, by the art; 'produces' is this, read from the cause) are in dependence_signature and dependences, read by no loop and no walk. 'Nothing is made without being worked', 'the makers must be made again' and 'production is by means of products', axioms of the earlier pour, are these dependences, and are no longer axioms. A way and a dependence on one pair are two facts of two kinds, and both are poured (v7 section 2.4). A dependence, like a way, is written where a source states it of the moment, and its reason names the kind it is said of.

The power to make, exercised in thought, is the plan: the architect raises his structure in imagination before he builds it (Marx I ch. 7). That is its own channel, 'is exercised in thought as', since what comes of it is a form held in mind, not the power in act. The plan is materialized as the product: the result that existed ideally at the beginning is realized in the material (Marx I ch. 7; Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b, the house with matter from the house without matter). The plan governs the working, which presupposes it (a dependence), and is not itself turned into the working. The dependence 'is conceived by' of the first v7 pour is withdrawn: no source states it apart from that exercise, and Aristotle's 'the art is the form' states a sameness.

One spelling names one way across Virgin Land's casts and lights (v7 section 2.2), and a channel is told by what passes and what comes back: 'is put to work as' is the lights' too. The surplus put to work is accumulation in its material form, written with 'is put to work as' and 'is consumed as'; Production writes no 'is invested as', which is Finance's commitment of money to a venture. Simple cooperation and the division of labour are two channels into the cooperation: joining workers in one process (Marx I ch. 13) and parting the work into detail operations (Smith I.1; Marx I ch. 14). Mechanization is one channel: the tool, the hand's operations, the divided operations and the makers' know-how built into a mechanism that performs them (Marx I ch. 15); the know-how is kept, its operations pass. Embodiment is labour spent into a bearer.

Every pair of moments was searched for an operation in the sources, and each one-step operation found is written. What a path through several comes to is read at the loops; the cast lists one-step operations only.

Marx's labour process (purposeful activity, the object of labour, the instruments) is the invariant of the concept, and the mode of production its variation, carried in the subject matter and not as a moment.

Labour objectified in a bearer is one channel, embodiment: the working embodied in the product and in the surplus, the work of reproduction in the makers' power (Seccombe 1974). Smith's and Marx's readings against the last are in open_forks.
Whether a product is an instrument or a material is settled by its function in the next making (Marx I ch. 7), so 'put to work' is one channel with either output.

The surplus is the working embodied past the necessary labour-time, which reproduces the value of the makers' power (Marx I ch. 9 section 1), however that share grows: by a longer working day (ch. 10) or by a shorter necessary time (ch. 12). In physical terms it is the net product, what the making leaves beyond the means used up and the makers' keep (Quesnay; Sraffa). The instrument reaches it only through the working it is set to. It is a moment, not an amount: the surplus product is a thing, the harvest beyond the seed and the sowers' food, with ways in (embodiment) and out (put to work, consumed); its size is a mark.

Reproduction is the work of making the makers again, feeding, raising and resting them, much of it the unpaid work of the household (Federici; Bhattacharya). The means replaced are the product put to work again.
The capacity is the makers' power; the soil and the earth are instruments of labour (Marx I ch. 7). The product is the thing made; whether a service is a product is in open_forks.

A bar means by no route in its word's channel (v7 section 2.3). One is written: the instrument is not worked into the product (Marx I ch. 8); it reaches the product only by being operated in the working, which is then embodied, another channel.

derived_check.ordering: by operation, read as directed: capacity -exercised in thought-> purpose -materialized-> product; capacity -exercised-> working and -> reproduction -embodied-> capacity, the household's circle; capacity -mechanized-> instrument; instrument -operated-> working; working -embodied-> product and surplus, -combined, -divided-> cooperation, -practised-> capacity, -mechanized-> instrument; cooperation -mechanized-> instrument and -embodied-> product, surplus; instrument -mechanized-> instrument; material -worked-> product; product -put to work-> instrument, material; product -consumed-> capacity; surplus -put to work-> instrument, material, -consumed-> capacity. Refused: instrument -worked into-> product (Marx I ch. 8). Dependences apart: the working requires the capacity, the material, the instrument and the product, and presupposes the purpose; the product is made of the material, has the form of the purpose, is made by the working and by the capacity; the capacity requires the product and the reproduction. Denied: the product is not made of the instrument (Marx I ch. 8). Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the instrument yield surplus? Written with Marx: it reaches the surplus only through the working it is set to (operated, then embodied); it passes on its own worth by wear and no more (I ch. 8), a count of value, not written as a way. The production function (Wicksteed 1894; Cobb and Douglas 1928) and Quesnay's net product of the soil are the other readings, with Sraffa's refusal to attribute the surplus to any factor.
Is the mode of production a moment or the frame of all the moments? Carried as the frame.
Is innovation (Schumpeter's new combination) a moment of production, or finance's doing through credit? Not written; a mark on the concept's history.
Is nature a co-producer (Moore 2015) or the material and the earth as instrument only? Written as the material and the instrument.
Is a service a product (Say) or an action with no product (Aristotle's praxis, Arendt)? The product is written as the thing made; a service is laid down in no thing (Smith, WN II.3).
Is cooperation a moment or a quality of the working? Kept as a moment.
Georgescu-Roegen's funds and flows: the capacity and the instrument are funds, the material a flow; carried in the glosses.

The plan as the capacity's exercise in thought (Marx's architect) or as the form the art already is (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7: the art of building is the form of the house)? Written with Marx, as a way of its own; read with Aristotle it would be a sameness, which a cast never writes.

Is the household's work laid down in the makers' power? Written with Seccombe (1974) and the social reproduction theorists. Smith (WN II.3) holds that menial labour fixes itself in no subject and perishes in the very act, and Marx (I ch. 6) counts in labour power's worth only the labour in the means of subsistence; the domestic labour debate of the 1970s left it open.
did_not_fit: The sale of the product: the market's, at the Production-Consumption edge.

The sharing of the product among persons is no act of making, so it is no way here. The allocation of the means and of the makers among the branches (Marx 1857 section 2: a moment of production itself) is the frame, the mode of production, which this cast carries in its subject matter and not as a moment (premise 6): the cast is the labour process.
The consumption of the product: consumption's, except the makers' individual consumption, which renews the capacity here.
Making money: finance's.
Art as making in the aesthetic sense: adjacent; a product that is not used.
Action (praxis), the other concept of doing: no corner of this run.
Nature untouched: the edge; nature worked is the material, and the earth used is an instrument.

Words left out because each is neither a way nor a dependence, or is another spelling of one written: 'settles as' (a shape); 'is left over as' (a subtraction, a partition of the product, not a channel: the surplus is reached by embodiment); 'is renewed as' (it puts being renewed on the reproduction, which does the renewing); 'is worn into' (the instrument passes on a part of its worth, a count of value); 'is fixed as' (folded into 'is embodied as'); 'is invested as' (Finance's commitment of money to a venture; the surplus put to work and consumed is written with 'is put to work as' and 'is consumed as'); 'is conceived by' (withdrawn: the plan is the capacity exercised in thought); 'is carried out as' (the plan governs the working, which presupposes it, and is realized in the product, 'is materialized as'); 'is productively consumed as' for the instrument (it is used up in the making by being operated, 'is operated as', and does not become the product, Marx I ch. 8; its wear is a count of value).
A relation whose term is no moment of this cast: 'belongs to' (the product and its owner): the owner is no moment here; it is distribution's title.

dependence_signature.meaning: the first cannot take place unless the second is there: the working and its conditions. A condition and what it conditions.
the first is what it is only given the second before it: purposeful activity and the purpose held in advance. A condition held in advance.
the first has the second as its matter: Aristotle's material cause.
the first has the second as its form: the house in matter and the house in the soul, Aristotle's formal cause.
the first has the second as its maker: the thing made and the making, Aristotle's efficient cause.

dependences.reason: labour is the use of labour power: no working without the power to work (Marx I chs. 6-7)
the simple elements of the labour process: purposeful activity, its object, its instruments (Marx I ch. 7)
the simple elements of the labour process (Marx I ch. 7); the instrument stands between the worker and the object
the result existed ideally at the beginning; the worker's purpose determines his mode of activity as a law (Marx I ch. 7)
that out of which a thing comes to be and which persists in it, the bronze of the statue (Aristotle, Physics II.3)
the house with matter comes from the house without matter, the form in the soul (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b)
the primary source of the change, the builder building (Aristotle, Physics II.3)
the owner of labour power must be able to renew it day by day: its maintenance requires a given quantity of the means of subsistence (Marx I ch. 6)
labour power is made and made again by the work of feeding, raising and resting the makers: no labour power without social reproduction (Bhattacharya ed. 2017, introduction; Federici 2004)
the builder builds in virtue of his art of building, and the art is the prior cause (Aristotle, Physics II.3 195b21-24)
products are not only results but essential conditions of labour (Marx I ch. 7); commodities are produced by means of commodities (Sraffa 1960 ch. 1)
the instrument passes into the product no matter: it keeps its own form apart from the product it helps make (Marx I ch. 8)

is exercised as.meaning: the first, exercised, is the second: the power in act is the working, or the work of the household. The way: exercise, the first becomes the second by being put into act.

is exercised in thought as.meaning: the first, exercised in the imagination before the work, is the second: the architect's power raising the structure in his head is the plan. The way: conception, the first becomes the second by being exercised in thought, and what comes of it is a form held in mind, not the power in act (Marx I ch. 7).

is materialized as.meaning: the first, given matter in the making, is the second: the house in the mind built is the house in stone; the result that existed ideally at the beginning, realized in the material. The way: materialization, the first becomes the second by its form's being put into matter (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b; Marx I ch. 7).

is mechanized as.meaning: the first, built into a mechanism that performs its operations, is the second: the tool fitted to a mechanism, the hand's motions, the divided operations and the makers' know-how taken over by the machine. The way: mechanization, the first becomes the second by its operations being built into a mechanism (Marx I ch. 15); the makers keep their skill, but its operations pass to the machine.

is worked into.meaning: the first, worked, is the second: the same matter in a new form, the ore in the iron. The way: working of matter, the first becomes the second by being shaped, the matter persisting.

is put to work as.meaning: the first, taken into a further making, is the second: as its means it is an instrument, as what the work is done on it is material; its function settles which. The way: putting to work, the first becomes the second by entering a making.

is embodied as.meaning: the first, objectified in a bearer, is the second: labour embodied in the thing made, surplus labour in the surplus product, the household's work in the makers' power. The way: embodiment, the first becomes the second by being laid down in a bearer that outlasts the act; the labour is spent in it.

is combined as.meaning: the first, joined with others' working side by side in one process, is the second: the working of many as one producer, simple cooperation. The way: combination of labour, the first becomes the second by being joined with others' in one place and time (Marx I ch. 13).

is divided as.meaning: the first, split into detail operations each done by another worker, is the second: the working of many as one producer, the pin factory's eighteen operations. The way: division of labour, the first becomes the second by being parted into operations and dealt out among workers (Smith I.1; Marx I ch. 14).

is practised into.meaning: the first, practised, is the second: labour repeated becomes skill, and the powers that slumber in the worker develop. The way: practice, the first becomes the second by repetition.

is operated as.meaning: the first, set in motion by living labour, is the second: the tool handled, the machine run, the pump going. The way: operation, the first becomes the second by being set going in the making.

is consumed as.meaning: the first, used up by the makers in living, is the second: the means of subsistence eaten and worn, from the product or the surplus, are the makers' power renewed or enlarged. The way: individual consumption, the first becomes the second by being consumed by the makers.

0.reason: the power exercised is the power in act: the use of labour power is labour itself (Aristotle, Metaphysics Theta.6-8; Marx I ch. 7)

1.reason: labour power spent in feeding, raising and resting the makers is the work of reproduction (Federici 2004; Bhattacharya ed. 2017)

2.reason: the architect raises his structure in imagination before he builds it in reality: the power to make, exercised in thought, is the plan (Marx I ch. 7)

3.reason: the skill and know-how of the makers built into the mechanism that performs their operations: the special skill of each operative vanishes before the science embodied in the factory mechanism (Marx I ch. 15 section 4); the accumulated knowledge and skill absorbed into fixed capital (Grundrisse, fragment on machines)

4.reason: at the end of the labour process a result emerges that existed ideally, in the worker's imagination, at its beginning: he realizes his purpose in the material (Marx I ch. 7); the house with matter comes from the house without matter (Aristotle, Metaphysics Z.7 1032b)

5.reason: the stuff worked is the thing made, the same matter in a new form: the ore is the iron, the timber the table (Aristotle, Physics I.7; Marx I ch. 7)

6.reason: labour fixes and realizes itself in a particular subject: the activity, finished, is the thing made (Smith, WN II.3; Hegel, Phenomenology 195; Marx I ch. 7)

7.reason: the working carried past the necessary labour-time, which reproduces the value of the makers' power, is surplus labour, laid down in surplus product (Marx I ch. 9 sections 1 and 4; chs. 10 and 12 on the two ways its share grows)

8.reason: the working of one, joined with others' side by side in one process, is the working of many as one producer: simple cooperation (Marx I ch. 13)

9.reason: the making of a pin split into some eighteen distinct operations, each done by another hand, is the working of many as one producer (Smith, WN I.1; Marx I ch. 14; Hegel, PR 198)

10.reason: by working the worker develops the powers that slumber in him; labour repeated becomes skill, as we become builders by building (Marx I ch. 7; ch. 14; Aristotle, NE II.1 1103a33)

11.reason: the operations of the working, made simple by division, built into a mechanism that performs them: the machine takes the tool from the worker's hand (Marx I ch. 15 section 1; Hegel, PR 198)

12.reason: the combination of detail workers, the subjective organism of manufacture, built into the objective organism of a system of machines (Marx I ch. 15 section 1)

13.reason: the collective worker's labour is laid down in its product (Marx I chs. 13-14)

14.reason: the collective worker's labour past the necessary labour-time is laid down in surplus product, and combination raises what that labour yields (Marx I ch. 9 section 1; ch. 13, the productive power of social labour)

15.reason: living labour seizes the instruments and awakens them from the dead: the instrument set going is the working (Marx I ch. 7)

16.reason: the tool, fitted to a mechanism that wields it, is the machine: the machine proper performs with its tools the operations the worker did with like tools (Marx I ch. 15 section 1)

17.reason: the instrument keeps its own form apart from the product it helps make and passes into it no matter, only value by wear (Marx I ch. 8): the material is worked into the product, the instrument is not

18.reason: a thing made becomes a means of further making: commodities by means of commodities (Marx I ch. 7; Sraffa 1960 ch. 1)

19.reason: raw material is itself the product of earlier labour: the yarn for the weaver, the seed for the sowing (Marx I ch. 7; Sraffa 1960)

20.reason: individual consumption converts the means of subsistence into newly reproduced labour power (Marx I ch. 23; ch. 6)

21.reason: surplus product put to work as additional means of production: accumulation in its material form (Marx I ch. 24)

22.reason: surplus product put to work as additional raw material (Marx I ch. 24)

23.reason: surplus product consumed as means of subsistence by additional makers is additional labour power: what is saved maintains more productive hands (Marx I ch. 24; Smith, WN II.3)

24.reason: the work of feeding, raising and resting the makers is laid down in their power to make again: domestic labour as labour embodied in labour power (Seccombe 1974; Federici 2004; Bhattacharya ed. 2017)

marks.gloss: the means of producing someone holds before any product is shared: the land, the capital, the money, the labour power one has to hire out
what a society's making yields, taken whole, before it is shared: Ricardo's produce of the earth, Marx's total social product, Marshall's national dividend
a claim to a portion made by contract in an exchange: the lease, the wage contract, the loan's interest, the bill, the bond's coupon; met by payment, and saleable unless the law forbids

a claim to a portion held by status, need or desert, under a standard or a membership: the citizen's right to a ration, the pension right, the poor's right to relief, the office by worth; not saleable
the giver's claim to a return for a gift accepted: the counter-gift due, the hospitality owed, the help to be returned; personal, met by a gift in turn (Mauss)
the standard by which portions are right portions: worth, need, equality, contribution, luck; Aristotle's axia, Rawls's difference principle, 'to each according to his needs'
a portion got of what there is: the wage, the rent, the interest, the profit, the dividend, named by their source; the ration, the benefit, the alms, named by their receiver
what a center gathers and holds to apportion: the tax revenue, the tribute, the temple's granary, the common store

axioms: Every portion is someone's; what is no one's is not yet distributed.
The measure of a right portion is not read off from the portions: what one gets does not say what one should get.
Where wealth accumulates the distribution makes its own excluded (Hegel, PR 243-245): a share of nothing is a point of the pattern.
A portion got by a claim, by gift, by trade or from a center is a portion all the same: the form of the apportioning does not change what is apportioned.
cast.subject: Distribution: the apportioning of what is produced, and of the means of producing, among the persons of a society: the produce to be shared, the holding that comes before any sharing, the claims through which a portion is owed, by contract, by entitlement and by gift, the measure by which a portion is right, the portion itself, and the store a center gathers to apportion from; with the ways the apportioning goes, by contract, by entitlement, by gift and its return, by trade, by inheritance, by force, from a center and by deduction; read from Aristotle, NE V.2-5; Hume, Treatise III.i.1 and III.ii.2-5; Smith, Wealth of Nations I.6-11, II.3 and V.2; Ricardo, Principles, preface; Paine, Agrarian Justice (1797); Hegel, Philosophy of Right 214 and 243-245; Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2, Capital I chs. 7, 24, 26-27 and III chs. 25, 48, 51, Critique of the Gotha Programme (1875); T. H. Marshall, Citizenship and Social Class (1950); Rawls, A Theory of Justice (1971); Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) ch. 7; Hayek, The Mirage of Social Justice (1976); Walzer, Spheres of Justice (1983); Polanyi, The Economy as Instituted Process (1957); Mauss, The Gift (1925); Sahlins, Stone Age Economics (1972); Piketty, Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2013)

file.concept: Distribution (the corner's name, given by Arman on 2026-10-19)
file.cast_by: Virgin Land, 2026-10-20, poured by MOLD v7 (adopted by Arman 2026-10-20; the Mothership's letter of 13:02) from the cast of the same morning in casts/mold-v6-norm_2026-10-20, which stays as the record. Under Arman's word of 2026-10-20: 'you are the user in this run, so you own all these kinds of decisions'.
premises: MOLD v7: a way-word names a way the first is turned into the second, by its channel; only IS says two are the same, and a cast never writes it. Dependence is poured apart in dependence_signature and dependences, read by no loop and no walk; a bar means by no route; one spelling names one way across Virgin Land's casts and lights. Every word in the signature is a transitive act done to the first moment; a state ('owned', 'kept', 'owed') or a naming ('priced') is not a way.

Lending money and letting a thing's use are two channels (Aquinas, ST II-II q.78: in the loan the money passes and its equivalent returns, in the letting the use passes and the thing returns), so the holding is lent as a claim when it is money, with Finance's spelling, and let out as a claim when it is land or labour power.

Dependences, apart: an entitlement presupposes the measure; the shares are determined by the holdings (Marx 1857), and the standard of right is bounded by them (Gotha); a share is a part of the produce; the produce requires the holdings and falls to the owner of the means (Marx I ch. 7), a title. A dependence, like a way, is written where a source states it of the moment, and its reason names the kind it is said of.

Every pair of moments was searched for an operation in the sources, and each one-step operation found is written. What a path through several comes to is read at the loops; the cast lists one-step operations only.

Polanyi's forms of integration, reciprocity, redistribution and exchange, are movements of goods (Polanyi 1957), so they are written as channels, not moments: giving, the acceptance that makes the receiver owe, and the reciprocation that meets it; pooling to a center and paying out from it; sale. The claims they make are three moments, since they come in, are met and may be sold in three ways: the claim by contract (exchange), met by payment, honoured; the entitlement by status, need or desert (redistribution), drawn on from the center's store; and the obligation of a gift (reciprocity), met by a gift in turn. Aristotle's corrective and distributive justice part the first two (NE V.2-5). The center's store is the fund.

A sale moves a holding or a claim from one person to another, and a gift a holding or a portion: sale runs from a holding to a holding and from a claim to a claim or to money, giving from a holding to a holding and from a portion to a portion. A portion reaches a person by a claim honoured, by an entitlement drawn on, by a gift of a portion or its return, or from a center.

The produce, what the making yields taken whole, is a moment: it is what is apportioned (Ricardo's principal problem). It has no way in here: it is made in production, and requires the holdings (a dependence). Its ways out are its parts set aside before division (Gotha): to the common store, pooled, and to the means, accumulated. It falls to the owner of the means (a title, a dependence), and a share is a part of it (a dependence); its division into wages, rent, interest and profit runs through the claims honoured and the owner's title. 'Is divided as' would be the genus of apportioning, and is not written.

Paying out from the center gives a portion or, as capital, a holding: one channel, since Paine pays the sum at majority and the pension from one fund. The holder of an entitlement draws on it: the same redistribution from the receiver's side, a channel of its own, since nothing passes from the one who draws. Two sides of one act are two channels wherever what passes differs.

The revenue (the portion named by its source: wage, profit, rent, interest) is the share under another name, and naming is no operation, so it is folded into the share's gloss. The pattern (the Gini, the top decile's share) is a reading of the shares, not a moment: no operation gives it but counting.
Distribution is poured as a concept of the economy and not as a theory of justice: the measure is one moment among others, and which measure is right is left to open_forks.
Marx's prior distribution, of the means of production among persons, is the holding.

A bar means by no route in its word's channel (v7 section 2.3). Two are written: the share is not inferred as the measure (Hume), and an entitlement is not traded as an entitlement (Walzer). No way of this cast runs into either second term by that word.

derived_check.ordering: by operation, read as directed: holding -let out, -lent-> claim -honoured-> share -accumulated-> holding, the circle of property; holding -sold, -given, -bequeathed, -expropriated-> holding; claim -sold-> claim and holding; measure -applied-> entitlement -drawn-> share and holding; share -accepted-> obligation -reciprocated-> share, and share -given-> share, reciprocity; holding, share and produce -pooled-> fund -paid out-> share and holding, redistribution; produce -accumulated-> holding. Refused: share -inferred-> measure (Hume); entitlement -sold-> entitlement (Walzer). The measure has no way in: no operation gives the standard, and the portions do not (the refusal); it is bounded by the holdings (Marx, Gotha), a dependence. The produce has no way in: it is made in production. Dependences apart: the entitlement presupposes the measure; the share is determined by the holding and the measure bounded by it; the share is a part of the produce; the produce requires the holding and falls to the owner of the holding. Marked derived.

open_forks: Does the market's outcome give the measure? Clark 1899 holds that each factor's marginal product is its just share, an identity more than an inference; Hayek 1976 ch. 9 denies that a catallaxy's outcome is just or unjust. The refusal written is Hume's, against inferring the measure from the portions.

Patterned or historical: Rawls makes entitlements from the measure applied (measure -> entitlement); Nozick makes holdings from acquisition and transfer (here trade, gift and bequest), with no measure presupposed. Original acquisition (Locke, Second Treatise 27) makes a holding of what was no one's and comes from outside the cast; rectification (Nozick ch. 7) and the jubilee are not written.

Profit: a share, the part of the produce that falls to the owner of the means (Ricardo; Marx I ch. 7 section 2), poured as two dependences, the share a part of the produce and the produce falling to the owner of the holding. Smith (WN I.6) and the trinity formula read profit as a revenue the stock itself yields; Marx (III ch. 48) denies it. That reading is not written, and neither is its denial; Marx's determination of the shares by the holdings (1857) is another dependence, and is written.
The revenue (the portion by its source) is folded into the share; Ricardo's 'principal problem', the laws of the functional distribution, is read on the shares, not written as a moment.
The pattern is written as a reading of the shares (see premises).

Polanyi sets each form on a supporting structure: symmetry for reciprocity, a center for redistribution, a price-making market for exchange. Only the center is a moment here (the fund); which form integrates an economy is not written. Hayek's catallaxy, many bargains without a center, is trade with no fund.
A gift's claim to a return is personal (Mauss). Whether it can pass to a third, as kula valuables pass on, is open, so no bar is written on trading the obligation.
Scope: the household, the state, or the world (Pogge, Beitz)? Not fixed by the cast.
Is a levy to a center pooling, or a taking by law of its own? Written as pooling, with Polanyi and Sahlins, who count levy and contribution as one movement to a center.

Hume's is and ought: written as a refused way, since his text speaks of a deduction, an operation that would take the portions and give the standard. Read as a denied dependence, the standard not resting on the portions, it would go to the dependences.
did_not_fit: The sale as a meeting of buyer and seller, and the price as the market's own act: at the Production-Consumption edge; here trade is the movement of holdings and claims only.
The production of what is shared: production's. The produce here is what it yields taken whole, before it is shared; the holding (Marx's prior distribution) is the contested boundary, kept here.
The consumption of the portion: consumption's.
Recognition and status apart from portions (Fraser 1995): outside.

Words left out because each is neither a way nor a dependence, or is another spelling of one written: 'is owned as' (the holding is already owned: an aspect; the act from holding to claim is letting or lending); 'is tallied as' (counting: the pattern is a reading); 'is priced as' (a portion named by its source: a classification); 'is paid for as' and 'is paid as' for the holding (the lease seen from the tenant's side: written once, as letting and honouring); 'is received as' (the revenue received is the same portion renamed); 'is kept as' (keeping a portion is laying it by as money, Finance's channel, or accumulating it as means, written here); 'is owed as' (owing is the receiver's side of acceptance, written once from the act); 'is traded as' (the sale, one channel with Finance's: 'is sold as'); 'is levied as' and 'is deducted as' (folded into pooling, one movement to a center); 'is granted as' (folded into paying out); 'is appropriated as' (a title, poured as the dependence the produce falls to the owner of the holding); 'is generalized as' (respelled 'is inferred as': Hume speaks of deduction); 'is divided as' (the genus of apportioning; its channels are written).

Relations whose terms are no moments of this cast: 'deserves' and 'earns' (the person's worth and the portion), 'is owed to' (the portion and its claimant), 'requires' (redistribution and a center). The person and the center are no moments here: the standard of worth is the measure, the person who has it is not; what the person reaches for is poured as the entitlement and its dependence on the measure, and the center's store is the fund.

The cover for replacing the means used up (Gotha's first deduction) restores the holding and changes no one's portion: simple reproduction (Capital I ch. 23), whose channel is production's putting to work. Not written here.

dependence_signature.meaning: the first is what it is only given the second before it: a claim by worth or need and the standard of worth or need. A condition held in advance. The same kind as Production's 'presupposes'.
the first takes its form and size from the second: the distribution of the products from the distribution of the means of production. A determination.
the first is a part cut from the second: a portion and the whole produce it is a portion of. A part and its whole.
the first cannot take place unless the second is there: the produce and the means it is made with. A condition and what it conditions. The same kind as Production's 'requires'.

the first is the property of whoever owns the second: the produce and the means it was made with; the owner of the means owns what is made with them, and its immediate producer does not. A title and what it rests on.
the first cannot rise above what the second allows: the standard of right and the economic structure that bounds it. A limit and what it limits.

dependences.reason: the just in distribution is according to worth of some sort: a claim by desert or need presupposes the standard (Aristotle, NE V.3 1131a); legitimate expectations are founded on the public rules of a just scheme (Rawls 1971 section 48)
the distribution of products is determined by the distribution of the instruments of production and of persons among the kinds of production (Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2; Capital III ch. 51)
right can never be higher than the economic structure of society and its cultural development conditioned thereby (Marx, Critique of the Gotha Programme, 1875, part I)

the produce of the earth is divided among the classes of the community as rent, profit and wages (Ricardo, Principles, preface); the whole price of the produce resolves into the three parts (Smith, WN I.6)

the produce of the earth is derived from its surface by the united application of labour, machinery and capital (Ricardo, Principles, preface); the distribution of the instruments of production is a moment of production itself (Marx, Introduction of 1857 section 2)
the product is the property of the capitalist and not that of the labourer, its immediate producer (Marx I ch. 7 section 2; ch. 24 section 1)

is let out as.meaning: the first, its use granted for a time on contract, is the second: the land let, the labour power hired is a claim to the price of its use. The way: letting, the first becomes the second by its use being granted against a price while the thing itself returns (the locatio).

is lent as.meaning: the first, handed over for a time against a promise to repay its equivalent, is the second: money owned, lent, is a claim to its return with interest. The way: lending, the first becomes the second by passing to the borrower against a promise of repayment (the mutuum). The same channel as Finance's 'is lent as'.

is sold as.meaning: the first, sold at a price, is the second: the holding or the claim sold is the buyer's, and the claim sold is money, a holding, in the seller's hands. The way: sale, the first becomes the second by passing to a buyer for money at a price; the change of hands and the seller's change of form are the two tuples one sale gives (Marx I ch. 3 section 2(a)). The same channel as Finance's 'is sold as'.

is given as.meaning: the first, handed over without price, is the second in the receiver's hands: the holding given, the portion shared. The way: giving, the first becomes the second by being transferred without price.

is bequeathed as.meaning: the first, passed on at death, is the second: the holding inherited is the heir's holding. The way: succession, the first becomes the second by being passed to an heir.

is expropriated as.meaning: the first, taken from its holders by force or by an act of enclosure, is the second in another's hands: the land enclosed, the commons taken, the tillers driven off. The way: expropriation, the first becomes the second by being taken from its holders without their consent and held by another (Marx I chs. 26-27). A levy to a center is pooling.

is pooled as.meaning: the first, a part of it gathered in by a center, by levy, by custom, or set aside from the whole before it is divided, is the second: the tax, the tithe, the tribute, the contribution, the deduction for common needs is the center's store. The way: pooling, the first becomes the second by passing to a center (Polanyi's redistribution, Sahlins's pooling, Marx's deductions from the total social product: one movement to a center).

is honoured as.meaning: the first, paid as it is owed, is the second: the claim by contract met is the portion. The way: honouring, the first becomes the second by being paid as owed. The same channel as Finance's 'is honoured as'; an entitlement is drawn on, and a gift's claim is met by reciprocation.

is applied as.meaning: the first, brought to a case, is the second: the standard applied to a person assigns that person's entitlement: by worth the office, by need the ration. The way: application, the first becomes the second by the universal standard's being made particular in a case (Hegel, PR 214). Not Consumption's 'is systematized as', which is another channel (a taste made the rule of every choice).

is accumulated as.meaning: the first, not consumed but added to the means of producing, is the second: the portion saved and employed, or the part of the produce set aside to enlarge the means, is capital for the next round. The way: accumulation, the first becomes the second by being added to what one holds as means. Not Finance's 'is laid by as', which withdraws money from circulation.

is accepted as.meaning: the first, a gift received and accepted, is the second: to accept is to owe, and the gift accepted is the giver's claim to a return. The way: acceptance, the first becomes the second by being taken as it is offered, which binds the one who takes it (Mauss), as a bill accepted binds its acceptor.

is reciprocated as.meaning: the first, met by a gift in turn, is the second: the giver's claim to a return, returned, is a portion in the giver's hands. The way: reciprocation, the first becomes the second by the one bound giving back (Mauss; Sahlins).

is paid out as.meaning: the first, paid out by the center, is the second: the store apportioned is the ration, the benefit, the pension; paid as capital, a holding. The way: paying out, the first becomes the second by being apportioned from the center's store (Polanyi's redistribution, from the center's side).

is drawn as.meaning: the first, drawn on by its holder, is the second: the right to a ration, a pension or relief, drawn on, is the portion; the right to a sum at majority, drawn, is a holding. The way: drawing, the first becomes the second by its holder's taking what the right gives from the center's store: redistribution from the receiver's side, where nothing passes from the one who draws.

is inferred as.meaning: the first, taken as a premise, would give the second as its conclusion: the standard of what one should get inferred from what one gets. Written only as refused. The way: inference from what is to what ought to be; Hume denies that any such deduction holds.

0.reason: the land let, the labour power hired: a holding's use granted on contract is a claim to its price (Smith, WN I.6, I.11: rent the price paid for the use of land; Hume, Treatise III.ii.5)

1.reason: money owned and lent is a claim to the interest of money lent, Smith's third revenue (Smith, WN I.6; II.4)

2.reason: a holding sold is the buyer's holding: transference by consent (Hume, Treatise III.ii.4; Nozick 1974 ch. 7, justice in transfer)

3.reason: a holding given between the living is the receiver's holding (Hume, Treatise III.ii.4; Piketty 2013 ch. 11, gifts counted with bequests)

4.reason: a holding passed at death is a holding again, the heir's: succession (Hume, Treatise III.ii.3; Piketty 2013 ch. 11)

5.reason: the land taken from its tillers is another's holding: the expropriation of the agricultural population, the enclosure of the commons (Marx I chs. 26-27)

6.reason: a part of a holding gathered by a center is the center's store: the land tax, the tribute in kind, the tax on capital (Smith, WN V.2; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5; Polanyi 1957)

7.reason: from the total social product, before it is divided, are set aside the reserve and insurance funds, the general costs of administration, what is for the common satisfaction of needs, and the funds for those unable to work (Marx, Critique of the Gotha Programme, 1875, part I)

8.reason: from the total social product is set aside an additional portion for the expansion of production (Marx, Critique of the Gotha Programme, 1875, part I; Capital I ch. 24)

9.reason: the claim met is the portion: the rent paid on the lease, the wage on the contract, the interest on the loan (Hume, Treatise III.ii.5, the performance of promises; Smith, WN I.6)

10.reason: a claim sold is the buyer's claim: bills passed on by endorsement, debts bought and sold (Marx III ch. 25; Hume, Treatise III.ii.4)

11.reason: a claim sold before its term is money in the seller's hands: bills and debts sold for cash (Marx III ch. 25)

12.reason: the right to a ration, a pension or relief, met by the center, is a portion: the social rights of citizenship paid (T. H. Marshall 1950; Rawls 1971 section 43, the transfer branch)

13.reason: every person's right, at majority, to a sum of capital from the national fund, paid 'not as charity but as a right' (Paine, Agrarian Justice, 1797)

14.reason: a right to relief, a pension right or an office held by worth cannot be sold: blocked exchanges (Walzer 1983 ch. 4). No way of this cast runs into the entitlement by sale.

15.reason: the gift returned, in kind or with increase, is a portion in the giver's hands: the obligation to reciprocate (Mauss 1925 chs. 1-2; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5)

16.reason: the standard applied to a case assigns a person's entitlement: the universal law made particular (Hegel, PR 214); rules applied to particular cases by judges and administrators (Rawls 1971 section 31); by need, the right to relief

17.reason: a portion not consumed but added to the means of producing is capital for the next round: whatever a person saves from his revenue he adds to his capital (Smith, WN II.3; Marx I ch. 24; Piketty 2013 ch. 11)

18.reason: a portion received as a gift and accepted is the giver's claim to a return: to accept is to owe (Mauss 1925 ch. 1; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5, balanced reciprocity)

19.reason: a part of a portion gathered by a center is the center's store: the tax on wages, rents and profits, the tithe, the contribution (Smith, WN V.2; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5; Polanyi 1957)

20.reason: a portion passed on without price is another's portion: the food shared in the household, the alms (Mauss 1925; Sahlins 1972 ch. 5, generalized reciprocity)

21.reason: what one gets does not say what one should get: an ought is no deduction from what is (Hume, Treatise III.i.1). No way of this cast runs into the measure.

22.reason: what the center pays out is a portion: the ration, the benefit, the pension (Polanyi 1957; 1944 ch. 4; Rawls 1971 section 43)

23.reason: a sum of capital paid from a national fund to every person at majority is a holding to begin with; the pension is paid from the same fund (Paine, Agrarian Justice, 1797)

marks.gloss: a lack the body or the life requires met: hunger, cold, shelter, the child's milk, the decent shirt; natural at its root, social in its form; filled, it is over until it returns
marks.source: Hegel, PR 190; Marx 1857 section 2; Smith, WN V.ii.k; Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus 127

marks.gloss: a lack the life does not require met: the longing for this rather than that before the purchase; Hegel's refined need, without a limit
marks.source: Hegel, PR 191; Campbell 1987 ch. 5

marks.gloss: the thing got at a cost: the purchase brought home, what the outlay buys from one's income or one's store
marks.source: Keynes, GT chs. 8-9; Miller 1998

marks.gloss: the thing put to what it is for: the shoe worn, the bread eaten, the book read, the tool used
marks.source: Aristotle, Politics I.9 1257a; Hegel, PR 59; Agamben 2014

marks.gloss: the pleasure a thing gives in its use: the need filled and felt as filled, the meal savoured, the warmth of the coat; the marginalist's utility
marks.source: Plato, Philebus 31d-32b; Gossen 1854; Scitovsky 1976

marks.gloss: the thing consumed to its end: the meal finished, the shoe worn out, the fuel burnt; Say's destruction of utility
marks.source: Say, Traite III.1; Arendt 1958 sections 13, 18

marks.gloss: consumption as a mark of who one is and where one stands: the refined, the plain, the conspicuous; the classifier that classifies the classifier
marks.source: Veblen 1899 chs. 3-6; Bourdieu 1979 chs. 1, 3; Baudrillard 1970 (sign-value)

marks.gloss: consumption settled into a pattern a person or class keeps: the standard of living, the household's habits
marks.source: Duesenberry 1949; Veblen 1899 ch. 5; Bourdieu 1979 ch. 3

marks.gloss: consumption destroyed in no use: the sacrifice, the feast's excess, the potlatch's destruction, the surplus burnt in glory; expenditure without material return
marks.source: Bataille 1933, 1949 ch. 1; Mauss 1925; Veblen 1899 ch. 4 (conspicuous waste)

axioms: Consumption is the end of production and its beginning again: what is used up calls for making.
A need has a limit; a want has none.
Buying is not enjoying: the enjoyment is in the use; what pleasure comes before it is the longing's own (Campbell 1987).
Every society has a surplus it cannot use, and spends it, in glory or in catastrophe (Bataille 1949).
What one consumes says what one is: taste classifies.
Consumption reproduces the need: the thing used up, the lack comes back (Marx, Introduction of 1857, section 2).
The thing used falls short of the longing that sought it, and the longing passes to a new object (Campbell 1987 ch. 5).
cast.subject: Consumption: the using of what is made to the point of using it up: the need and the want, the thing got at a cost, the thing put to its use, the need filled and enjoyed, the thing used up, and the social forms of use, taste and the style of life, and the spending destroyed in no use; read from Plato, Philebus 31d-32b; Aristotle, Politics I.9; Hume, Of the Standard of Taste; Rousseau, Discourse on Inequality II; Smith, Wealth of Nations II.3 and V.ii.k; Say, Traite III; Hegel, Philosophy of Right 59 and 190-195; Marx, Manuscripts of 1844 ('The Power of Money'), Introduction of 1857 section 2 and Capital I ch. 6; Gossen (1854); Veblen, The Theory of the Leisure Class (1899); Bataille, The Notion of Expenditure (1933) and The Accursed Share (1949); Duesenberry, Income, Saving and the Theory of Consumer Behavior (1949); Bourdieu, Distinction (1979); Campbell, The Romantic Ethic and the Spirit of Modern Consumerism (1987); Arendt, The Human Condition (1958); Agamben, The Use of Bodies (2014)
